Do not commit anything, do not modify tracked files except temporarily for instrumentation, and revert any such edits when done. Scratch files go in /private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/28d33b5a-3e97-48b6-8eaf-5192f6d7d30d/scratchpad.

Goal: measure how long a full project export (the "restorable copy" the Agent panel timeline takes) costs on the UI thread, and how big the file is, for realistically large models. Today the only number is "about 170 ms and 31 KB on a small two-plate test project" from an earlier phase. We need numbers for real mesh sizes.

What to measure:
1. Wall-clock of `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::export_project_archive` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp, around line 378) or equivalently `ProjectPersistence::capture_revision` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp, around line 303; it already records `m_stats.last_capture_ms`). Report milliseconds and output file size.
2. For at least three model sizes: roughly 5 MB, 20 MB, and 50 MB of mesh data loaded into the project (a single high-resolution mesh is fine; a sphere or a subdivided cube generated with libslic3r, or any large STL you find under resources/ or tests/). State the triangle counts.
3. Separately, a fact-finding question for a hypothesis: could the export run on a worker thread from a copy of `Slic3r::Model`? Determine from the code whether copying a `Model` / `ModelObject` / `ModelVolume` / `TriangleMesh` deep-copies the mesh buffers (`indexed_triangle_set`) or shares them, and roughly how long a Model copy takes for the 20 MB case if you can measure it cheaply. Report what the code does; do not speculate.

How to run it:
- Read these memory notes first: /Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/jusprin-worktree-build.md, live-test-built-app-on-mac.md, bash-cwd-resets-after-background.md, track-wall-clock-on-background-work.md.
- The macOS build is in build/arm64 (cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target <target>). Check whether it is already configured with BUILD_TESTS=ON before assuming test targets exist.
- Prefer the existing harnesses: tests/workspace/ (workspace harness) and tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp with src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md. Look at how the earlier 170 ms number was produced (grep agent-docs/jusprin and tests/ for "capture", "last_capture_ms", "benchmark") and reuse that path if it exists. Use an isolated --datadir; never drive another running JusPrin instance.
- If the only practical route is a small Catch2 test or harness scenario that loads a generated mesh and calls the export, write it under the scratchpad or as an untracked file and delete it afterwards.
- Long builds: run them in the background and verify they are progressing (ps CPU time), do not trust a completion notification blindly.

Report back, in plain English for someone who did not see this session: a table of model size, triangle count, export ms, file bytes; whether the export is on the UI thread; what Model copy does with mesh buffers and any copy timing; exactly how you measured (commands, files); and anything that made the numbers unreliable.

Before writing any fix:

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Rules to follow every time:


`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata:

  modified: 2026-09-09T16:51:11.156Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

While working in a git worktree, a later `cmake --build build/arm64` and a
`git status` ran in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (the main checkout)

metadata:

During Phase 4 (2026-08-30), a background build "ran" for 5 hours: the
machine slept, the build paused, the 10-minute task timeout never fired, and
no completion notification arrived. I sat waiting instead of noticing.

**Why:** Background-task notifications are not guaranteed (sleep, wedged
timeouts). A silent wait looks identical to progress.

**How to apply:** For any background job expected to take more than a couple
of minutes: (1) check `date` and the process's CPU-time (`ps`) when resuming
work — near-zero CPU over long wall-clock means stalled or slept, not
working; (2) prefer a bounded Monitor (until-loop + explicit timeout) over
waiting for completion notifications; (3) when the user returns after a gap,
re-verify liveness of anything left running before reporting status.

## Result: full project export cost vs mesh size

All numbers are from `build/arm64` **RelWithDebInfo**, which this repo compiles at **-O0** (`CMakeLists.txt:544-548` rewrites `-O2` to `-O0` for Clang). The shipping Release config is -O3 and was not built (empty `build/arm64/src/*/Release/`; a full -O3 build is roughly an hour). Treat the absolute milliseconds as an upper bound; the ratios and the "where the time goes" split are what to trust. The earlier "170 ms / 31 KB" figure came from the same -O0 harness config, so it is comparable.

Machine: Apple M2 Pro, 12 cores, 32 GB, macOS 26.3. One sphere mesh per project, one plate, the default Bambu X1C profile from `tests/data/jusprin/harness.conf`. "Mesh size" = binary STL bytes (50 B/triangle); the in-memory `indexed_triangle_set` is about a third of that.

| Mesh (STL) | Triangles | `export_project_archive` ms (3 runs) | 3MF bytes | Serialization only (`store_bbs_3mf`, no thumbnails) | 3MF bytes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 MB (baseline) | 1,980 | 120 / 121 / 121 | 88,886 | 25 ms | 37,405 |
| 5.0 MB | 100,172 | 1,054 / 1,059 / 1,055 | 1,223,539 | 936-942 ms | 1,149,231 |
| 20.0 MB | 400,056 | 3,757 / 3,748 / 3,727 | 4,621,424 | 3,593-3,620 ms | 4,554,866 |
| 49.9 MB | 998,000 | 8,337 / 8,356 / 8,350 | 9,347,393 | 8,255-8,312 ms | 9,285,383 |

Findings:
- **Cost is linear, about 8.3-10.5 ms per 1,000 triangles at -O0.** A 1M-triangle project blocks the UI for ~8.3 s per timeline row; a 100k one for ~1 s.
- **The export is on the UI thread.** `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::export_project_archive` asserts `wxIsMainThread()` (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:378`) and the harness confirmed `main_thread=1`; `ProjectPersistence::capture_revision` calls it synchronously from the workspace-change handler (`ProjectPersistence.cpp:172, 303-315`).
- **Almost all of it is mesh serialization, not thumbnails.** Thumbnail rendering + `publish()` + plate bookkeeping is a fixed ~95-140 ms (the 2k-triangle case: 120 ms total vs 25 ms store-only; this matches the old 170 ms for a two-plate project = 2 plates x 4 GL thumbnails). Everything above that is `_BBS_3MF_Exporter::_add_mesh_to_object_stream` (`bbs_3mf.cpp:7142`) writing vertices/triangles as XML text through `format_coordinate`, then deflating at `MZ_DEFAULT_LEVEL` (`bbs_3mf.cpp:6751`). For 1M triangles the uncompressed model part is 82.8 MB of text, compressed to 9.3 MB; the PNG thumbnails are ~60 KB.
- A second run with two harness instances overlapping (see caveats) gave the same numbers within 1%, so they are stable.

## Model copy: mesh buffers are shared, not deep-copied

Verified in code and measured:
- `ModelVolume` holds `std::shared_ptr<const TriangleMesh> m_mesh` (`Model.hpp:1040`) and its copy constructor is `= default` (`Model.hpp:1030`), so copying shares the buffer. `Model::assign_copy` -> `ModelObject::new_copy` -> `ModelObject::assign_copy` -> `new ModelVolume(*volume)` (`Model.cpp:59-110, 1121-1160`) never touches mesh data. `TriangleMesh` itself holds `indexed_triangle_set its` by value (`TriangleMesh.hpp:158`), so copying a *TriangleMesh* is a deep copy.
- Measured `Model copy(plater.model())`: **0.13 ms (100k), 0.20 ms (400k), 0.25 ms (1M)**; after the copy `mesh_ptr()` of source and copy are the same pointer (`mesh_ptr_shared=1`). A deliberate deep `TriangleMesh` copy costs 0.5 / 2.2 / 6.3 ms respectively, so even a fully private copy would be cheap.
- Mutation paths are copy-on-write in the normal case: `ModelVolume::transform_this_mesh` builds a new `TriangleMesh` and `set_mesh`es it (`Model.cpp:2896-2900`). Two exceptions mutate through `const_cast` in place: `center_geometry_after_creation` (`Model.cpp:2606`) and `scale_geometry_after_creation` (`Model.cpp:2886`, commented "could only be called before the meshes ... are shared"). Both are creation-time paths; a worker export would need to be started after them, or from a deep copy.
- Hypothesis probe: `store_bbs_3mf` run on a `std::thread` from the shared-mesh `Model` copy, with `store_to_3mf_structure` plate data and `full_config_secure()` taken on the UI thread first, produced byte-identical archives (1,149,231 / 4,554,866 / 9,285,383 bytes) at the same speed as on the main thread (944 / 3,590 / 8,288 ms). `bbs_3mf.cpp` references no `wxGetApp`/GUI globals. This is one successful run, not a thread-safety proof; the thumbnails (the fixed ~100 ms) must stay on the GL/UI thread.

## How it was measured

- Temporary harness `export_bench_harness.cpp` (kept at `/private/tmp/claude/.../scratchpad/export_bench_harness.measured-copy.cpp`), modeled on `tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp`: boots `GUI_App` with an isolated temp `--datadir` + `harness.conf`, waits for `GLCanvas3D::is_initialized()`, then per size: `new_project`, `its_make_sphere(50, 2*pi/sqrt(N))`, `its_write_stl_binary`, `Plater::load_files`, center on plate 0, `reload_scene`, then 3x `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::export_project_archive`, 3x direct `store_bbs_3mf` with the same `SaveStrategy` (Silence|SplitModel|ShareMesh|SkipAuxiliary|Zip64) and no thumbnails, 3x `Model` copy, 3x `TriangleMesh` copy, 1x worker-thread store. Timing via `steady_clock` around the call, sizes via `file_size`.
- Built by temporarily appending an `add_executable(export_bench_harness ...)` block to `tests/workspace/CMakeLists.txt` (`cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target export_bench_harness`); that edit is reverted, `git status` is clean, and the harness bundles were deleted from `build/arm64/tests/workspace/*/`. Because the CMakeLists revert changed its mtime, the next `cmake --build build/arm64` will re-run CMake once (the generated ninja still names the target until then); the earlier re-run rebuilt the PCH and the whole RelWithDebInfo tree (48 min), so budget for that.

## Things that made the numbers less reliable

1. **-O0 build.** Explained above; the most important caveat for an absolute UI-thread budget.
2. **Load time is also huge:** `load_files` took 5.2 s / 20 s / 49 s for the same meshes at -O0, which suggests the same order-of-magnitude penalty applies to the export figures.
3. **A first version of the harness livelocked** (self-reposting `CallAfter` poll starving the nested `YieldFor` in WebView creation; the exact trap documented at `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:2838`); it was replaced by a one-shot `wxTimer` poll. During one measured run a stuck copy of the old harness was spinning one core; a clean rerun on a quiet machine matched it within 1%, and the clean run's numbers are the ones in the table.
4. **A second harness process appeared from the same scratchpad** (launched with `timeout 560`, and the scratch source was edited and the CMake edit reverted while this session ran) — apparently a parallel copy of this task. Its results equal the clean rerun; nothing else was driven, and no instance that this session did not start was killed.
5. The harness process segfaults at exit after `HARNESS RESULT PASS` (exit 139), the known inherited teardown crash with volumes loaded; it does not affect the measurements.
6. Only one plate, one object, a single-vendor profile, no painting or per-object config; multi-plate projects add ~100 ms of thumbnails per plate, and multiple objects serialize each mesh separately.
